items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: we did a rehearsal with Sammy Price.

ctx.x: Now how Sammy Price came into the picture, it was like this. We were looking for a piano player. So Sammy Price was playing piano at that time, pretty good! And so in -- in this audition he had invited us to his house, and his mother had fixed sandwiches and cold drinks and everything for us while she was away, we did a rehearsal with Sammy Price.

Well, this sounds funny, because Sammy has now become to be a big star, but at that time we figured he was not good enough for our band, and so we drank him up, lemonade and whatnot, ate all his food, rehearsed at his house, and then told him we were very sorry, that we couldn't use him.

items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: But when I got to Chicago I knew a lot of people. Budd Johnson was there

ctx.x: I still remember how nice he was to me and I think this is what make me, you know, kind to people. If I see a person on the highway, if I can help, or...well, actually, I believe, though, that this kind of feeling that I have for helping people became more when my wife became ill, because after having a four year experience with my wife being ill from '74 to '78, then I had, you know, I created that soft spot in my heart... it really came to the fore. And I just really...I'm an old man myself, but I help old…

But when I got to Chicago I knew a lot of people. Budd Johnson was there and other jazz musicians, you know, because they didn't all stay in the same place, they'd move around. So I knew Jesse Stone...oh, Jesse Stone was in Kansas City. Do you know about him?
He was a fine arranger, wasn't he?
